clue.text: Journeyed from American island to speak

indicators.note: to speak means the island's name is said out loud, and the spelling is set aside

blocks.note: Rhode Island is the smallest US state

explanation.surface: A traveller describes setting out from an American island to give a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhode Island and RODE are said the same way; only the spelling differs.
explanation.definitionFit: Rode is the past tense of ride, a way of having travelled on horseback or by vehicle.

clue.text: Give a new interpretation of advice, once excellent

blocks.note: rede is an archaic word for counsel; 'once' marks it as old
fine means excellent

explanation.surface: Someone reinterprets advice that used to be very good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' looks as if it goes with excellent, but it tells you the word for advice is an old one.
explanation.definitionFit: To redefine something is to explain or describe it afresh, giving it a new meaning.

clue.text: Take a chance, as prolific artist

blocks.note: first meaning: decide something by picking straws or tickets at random
second meaning: what a prolific artist does, producing many pictures

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful literal reading of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Settling something by random selection of tokens is the idiom, while a busy illustrator makes a great many sketches.

clue.text: Cavalier returns no bow — fret about this

indicators.note: something that returns comes back the way it went, so the little word is read right to left
about means going round, so the word for fret wraps around what comes before it

blocks.note: a sea fret is a coastal mist in north-east England and Scotland
taken as written
a bow is a curved shape, an arch

explanation.surface: A dashing courtier refuses to bow and someone worries about the snub.
explanation.walkthrough: Fret reads as worry, but it is the noun for a sea mist. 'This' points back to the reversed word plus the bow, which the mist goes round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cavaliers were the Royalist side in the English Civil War, supporters of the king and so of monarchy.

clue.text: Ancient, or 17

indicators.note: 17 down is a word for losing one's head, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: or is the heraldic term for gold, so golden

explanation.surface: An ancient person, or one who lost their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like a conjunction but is the heraldic colour gold; the cross-reference to 17 tells you to take its head off.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden is a literary word for belonging to long ago, as in olden days.

clue.text: City school-teacher puts head down on block

indicators.note: the leading letter is moved one place lower, which rearranges the word

blocks.note: a schoolmaster is a teacher
a dam blocks a river

explanation.surface: A teacher rests his head on a desk.
explanation.walkthrough: The teacher's first letter drops one place, behind the second; 'block' reads as a desk or a chopping block but is a barrier on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Amsterdam is the capital city of the Netherlands.

clue.text: Needled, being stuck in house over holiday, one gets all lit up

definitions.text: Needled, being stuck in house over holiday, one gets all lit up

blocks.clueFragment: Needled, being stuck in house over holiday
blocks.note: surface reading: someone irritated at being cooped up indoors during the break
setter's reading: a conifer with needles brought indoors for the December festival and hung with lights

explanation.surface: An annoyed person, trapped at home all holiday, ends up getting drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Needled means annoyed and lit up means drunk in the surface; literally the needles are pine needles and the lights are fairy lights.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorated fir stands indoors over the festive season, covered in strings of lights.

clue.text: Old raiders not at first appearing in history book

indicators.note: not at first means the opening letter is missing

blocks.note: the Vikings were Norse seafaring raiders

explanation.surface: Ancient raiders absent from the start feature in a history book.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is read as 1 Kings, with the I as the numeral one.
explanation.definitionFit: The First Book of Kings is one of the historical books of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Start to hunt through odds and ends of things for a garment

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter
the odds are the letters in odd-numbered places
the ends of a word are its first and last letters
going through means passing inside, so the single letter sits between the other parts

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters
first letter
first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone begins rummaging through bits and pieces for something to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odds and ends' reads as clutter, but it takes two sets of letters from the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tights are a close-fitting garment covering the legs and lower body.

clue.text: The hard stuff suited one

blocks.note: first meaning: the hardest natural mineral
second meaning: a playing card of one of the four suits

explanation.walkthrough: The hard stuff sounds like strong liquor, but here it is the gemstone; suited one is a card from a deck.
explanation.definitionFit: The gem is famed as the hardest substance in nature, and one of the four card suits shares its name.

clue.text: Loveliest daughter was ruined, making false accounts

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, and its pieces lie in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for daughter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A beautiful daughter's ruin leads to lying stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was' reads as part of the verb 'was ruined', but it belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Old wives' tales are traditional beliefs passed on as fact but untrue.

clue.text: Enjoying the waves? One shortly holds evidence of shark

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter of the word for one wave is dropped
to hold something is to have it inside, so the shark evidence sits within

blocks.note: one of the waves just mentioned: a surge
a fin cutting the water is the sign a shark is near

explanation.surface: A swimmer enjoying the sea spots a shark's fin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' refers back to the waves: a single wave is a surge. The question mark flags that the definition is a playful description.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding breaking waves on a board is the sport, a lively way of enjoying the sea.

clue.text: From traditional entertainment, fan locked out

indicators.note: out here means out of order, so these letters are put into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A devotee is shut out of a traditional show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locked out' reads as a phrase about a barred fan; 'out' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance handed down through a community's customs, such as morris, is a traditional entertainment.

clue.text: A lot of sense

blocks.note: first meaning: a great deal, as in 'a ___ better'
second meaning: the faculty of the eyes

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as 'plenty of good sense'; split it after 'A lot' and each half is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the word means a large amount, and it is also vision, one of the five senses.

clue.text: Be unconcerned with what Gable told Leigh he did, frankly

definitions.text: what Gable told Leigh he did, frankly

blocks.note: first meaning: be completely indifferent

blocks.clueFragment: what Gable told Leigh he did, frankly
blocks.note: second meaning: Clark Gable's famous last line to Vivien Leigh in Gone with the Wind

explanation.walkthrough: As Rhett Butler, Gable tells Leigh's Scarlett 'Frankly, my dear, I don't give a damn'; 'frankly' quotes the line's opening word.
explanation.definitionFit: Not caring in the slightest is the idiom's meaning, exactly the indifference Rhett declares.

clue.text: I hit boxer violently in shower

indicators.note: acting violently throws things about, so these letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to attacking a boxer in a bathroom shower.
explanation.walkthrough: Shower is not the bathroom fitting but one who shows.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhibitor puts goods or work on public display, so is one who shows.

clue.text: There’s calculated psychological pressure in chess, for example

blocks.note: first meaning: deliberate manipulation to unsettle someone
second meaning: a contest of thought rather than physical skill

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one statement about chess tactics, but it holds two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for psychological manipulation, and literally a game of the intellect such as chess.

clue.text: Fatally cut Howard’s End

definitions.note: names the fate itself, a noun phrase for what the adjective describes

blocks.note: first meaning: executed by losing one's head
second meaning: how Catherine Howard, Henry VIII's fifth wife, died in 1542

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like E. M. Forster's novel Howards End, but it is the death of Catherine Howard at the Tower of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Decapitation kills, and it was the method of execution used on Henry VIII's queen Catherine Howard.

clue.text: State London borough has empty properties to rent

indicators.note: an empty word has had its inside removed, so only its outside letters are kept

blocks.note: Newham is a borough in east London
the word's first and last letters
to hire something is to rent it

explanation.surface: A London council owns vacant buildings it lets out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb but is the definition, a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the six New England states of the USA.

clue.text: Sees it coming? Not altogether; this could be fun

indicators.note: not altogether means not every letter is kept, so parts of the words are dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone half anticipates something that might turn out to be enjoyable.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the start of each word survives: one letter, then two, then three.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation comedy is a television show meant to amuse, so a source of fun.

clue.text: Mace, a weapon raised — about time I left

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word lifts it bottom to top, so it reads backwards
the letter I has left, so it is taken out of the word for time
about means around, so the weapon goes round the shortened word

blocks.note: a gun is a weapon
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mace, a weapon held aloft, and someone saying it is time they went.
explanation.walkthrough: Mace looks like the club weapon the surface describes, but it is the spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Mace is a spice made from the lacy covering of the nutmeg seed, so the two are closely linked.

clue.text: Into Brazil, say, one following another Northerner

indicators.note: going into a word means being placed inside it
following means coming after, so the first one stands in front of the rest

blocks.note: another one, a second I
a Brazil is a kind of nut; 'say' marks it as an example
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone heads into Brazil, one traveller trailing another from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Brazil is not the country but the nut; one I goes inside it and a second I stands in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit are the indigenous peoples of the Arctic, so a member is a far northerner.

clue.text: Man who made report, sounding in drink

indicators.note: sounding means as it sounds, so the word for drink is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: a beverage is any drink

explanation.surface: A man who filed a report is heard speaking while drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' suggests a gunshot or a news story; it is William Beveridge's 1942 report, the blueprint for Britain's welfare state.
explanation.definitionFit: Economist William Beveridge wrote the 1942 report that led to the National Health Service and social security.

clue.text: Come to see a bomb’s what is needed

blocks.note: the V1 was a German flying bomb, with the 1 read as I; add the 's
'it' is the very thing wanted, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: Visitors are told a bomb is exactly what is required.
explanation.walkthrough: The V1 was a flying bomb fired at London in 1944; the digit 1 stands in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To visit someone is to go to see them.

clue.text: Arrived by chance in court

blocks.note: came means arrived
one's lot is one's fortune, what chance gives

explanation.surface: Someone turned up at a court of law by accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrived by chance' reads as one phrase, but it is two pieces; 'court' is a royal court, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: Camelot is King Arthur's legendary castle and the seat of his royal household.

clue.text: Waiter brings meat course, then runs through bill

indicators.note: running through something means passing inside it, so the runs go within the bill

blocks.note: a stew is a meat dish served as a course
a bill is a poster, an advertisement
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A waiter serves the main course and then the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill reads as the restaurant bill, but here it is a posted notice, an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward serves food and drink on a ship or aircraft, so a kind of waiter.

clue.text: I say Margaret is not gay, your worship

indicators.note: I say means the speaker is talking aloud, so what follows is heard

blocks.note: Maggie is short for Margaret, and straight means not gay

explanation.surface: Someone tells a magistrate in court that Margaret is not gay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say' looks like an exclamation of surprise but signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: In England a magistrate on the bench is addressed in court as 'Your Worship'.

clue.text: Darling girl shortly has to travel

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the name loses its last letter

blocks.note: Wendy Darling is the girl in Peter Pan

explanation.surface: A sweetheart must soon go away.
explanation.walkthrough: Darling reads as a term of endearment, but it is the family surname in Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: To wend is to go or travel, as in wending one's way.
